notes:
Topline: mid-market multi-tenant SaaS (customer success/product analytics) building an embeddable agent platform. Evaluating Redwood Hosted first (fast path) then Dedicated for predictable throughput and tenant isolation.

Key business/tech points: 
- Primary workload: multi-tenant chat agents (support assistants), lots of short-turn conversations + occasional long tool-driven responses (external API enrichments).
- Latency is a top priority: customers measure perceived latency on streaming token arrival. They want 95p <=150ms for single-turn responses; currently seeing 95p ~220ms on Hosted in our POC (needs improvement).
- Streaming stability: intermittent chunking/jitter when tool-calls return large JSONs; they use function-calling pattern and stream parsed tokens to client. Report: "we get a noticeable pause when the tool returns, then a burst of tokens".
- Rate limiting: per-tenant quotas and burst controls required. Billing team needs token-level metering + per-route rules per tenant. Target burst 100 rps per tenant, but want to test behavior under multi-tenant noisy-neighbor scenarios.
- Model preferences: prefer medium-sized open models (cost-sensitive) for regular tenants, auto-fallback to larger/slow but more capable models for premium tenants. Interested in Redwood recommendations on quantization and batching to hit latency/cost goals.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required for Dedicated. Also need SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, and audit logs for tooling access. Data residency: subset of EU customer data must remain in EU region (may trigger Private or Dedicated placement).

POC notes & results:
- Setup: quick onboarding to Hosted API; created per-tenant routing mock, integrated tool-calls to internal CRM.
- Observed: 95p latency 200-250ms for short replies; 99p spikes when cache misses happen. Streaming jitter when tool-call payloads >2KB.
- Workarounds tested: prefix caching reduced some traffic but not tool-call burst; increasing streaming window helped but increased token cost.

Sales/Commercial:
- Interested in price break for committed Dedicated capacity vs hosted per-token for stable tenants.
- Wants clear migration path: hosted -> dedicated with same API surface and rollout controls.
- Asks: SLA for 95p latency tiers, per-tenant quotas, how Redwood handles noisy tenants and circuit-breakers.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- Head of Product: "We need streaming to feel instant — even a small pause kills conversion."
- Infra lead: "If we can't get predictable 95p latency, we'll have to build more edge caching ourselves."

Next actions: 
- SE to run targeted perf tests (Diego) on hosted with smaller model + batching/quant profiles (due 2026-02-28).
- If 95p target not met, scope 1-week Dedicated POC with reserved capacity and custom routing.
- Procurement & legal: get SOC2 report and draft SOW for Dedicated (timeline depends on SOC2 availability).

Open questions for Redwood:
- Can Redwood surface per-tenant quotas and dynamic throttles out-of-the-box?
- Exact streaming behavior with function calls and chunked tool outputs — can we attach tracing to streaming segments?
- Pricing for committed Dedicated with mixed model sizes across tenants (tiered billing).

Internal notes: watch for noisy-neighbor tests during perf run; collect full token-level traces and streaming segment logs. Attach Fireflies transcripts for call notes.
